title: Sable and the Atlas
premise: In 1923, apprentice clockmaker Rosalind Nakamura is summoned to a mountain observatory to repair its failing master clock, only to find the town's records — and the observatory's astronomer, Elias Sable — entangled in a cover-up of a surveyor's death that the coming colonial administration wants buried. When the season's first snows close the bridge, Rosalind is trapped among the very people rewriting history, and her precision with time becomes the town's only weapon: the clock's escapement holds a hidden ledger of the truth. As she and Elias fall in love across the fault line of duty and memory, she must choose between the guild that raised her and the record that must survive. The book ends with Rosalind testifying before the victors' historians, the restored master clock striking as her evidence is entered on the record — at the exact hour it was always meant to strike.
about_author: Emrys Ishikawa is the pen name of a former horologist's apprentice who spent a decade restoring tower clocks in coastal towns before turning to fiction. Their work explores what instruments — and people — remember when institutions would rather they forget.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. In the guild workshop, Rosalind receives the summons to the mountain observatory and her master's warning: repair the clock, ask nothing about the records room. She packs her tools, measuring her life by what fits in one case. Emotional beat: quiet ambition shadowed by the sense of being sent as someone else's instrument.

chapters.title: Ascent by Switchback
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The climb to the observatory introduces the town of Veymar, its mixed community, and the surveyor's empty house with its boarded windows. A child tells her the master clock 'lies at midnight.' Emotional beat: unease arriving ahead of her, like weather.

chapters.title: The Astronomer Who Keeps Hours No One Asked For
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She meets Elias Sable, who greets her with suspicion and a list of forbidden rooms. Their first sparring match over the clock's mechanism reveals he knows more than an astronomer should. Emotional beat: reluctant fascination; two precise people circling each other.

chapters.title: Escapement
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Opening the master clock, she finds the escapement deliberately altered — someone has been making it lose exactly four minutes a night. She restores it without reporting the tampering. Emotional beat: first complicity; the thrill and guilt of a secret kept in brass.

chapters.title: What the Surveyor Measured
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Flashback woven into present: the surveyor Anselm charted the valley's true borders, findings that contradict the annexation maps. His death was ruled accidental. Elias has been hiding the original plates inside the observatory dome. Emotional beat: grief calcified into vigilance.

chapters.title: Four Minutes Past Midnight
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. At midnight the corrected clock strikes, and the whole town seems to flinch. The magistrate visits, all courtesy and threat, asking whether the clock now 'keeps official time.' Emotional beat: Rosalind realizes her repair was heard as a declaration.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. First snow seals the bridge; the last courier leaves carrying sealed orders no one will name. Rosalind is trapped until spring, officially a guest, practically a hostage of the season. Emotional beat: claustrophobia — the story's walls close like a case around a movement.

chapters.title: Tea at the Edge of the Dome
chapters.summary: Elias and Rosalind's shared POV alternation. Snowbound evenings over tea and star charts become confession-adjacent conversations neither will finish. He shows her the stars used to verify Anselm's coordinates. Emotional beat: intimacy growing in the space duty leaves unguarded.

chapters.title: The Guild's Letter
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A letter arrives via the last sled: her master instructs her to certify the clock 'as found' and return. Certifying means endorsing the falsified time — and the falsified maps it anchors. Emotional beat: love against duty takes shape; her hands shake for the first time over a simple form.

chapters.title: Anselm's Widow
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She visits the widow Marta, who recognizes the clockmaker's mark on Rosalind's loupe and gives her Anselm's field notebook, half-burned. Emotional beat: inheritance of grief; Rosalind stops being a bystander and becomes a keeper.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Escapement
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He reveals the full mechanism: Anselm hid micro-etched data on the escapement wheel itself, trusting only a clockmaker could read it. Only Rosalind can decode it — and only if the wheel stays intact while everyone wants it replaced. Emotional beat: awe and terror; the truth has been ticking overhead all along.

chapters.title: Inspection
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The colonial inspector arrives early, before the thaw, escorted over the pass. He orders the master clock dismantled and shipped to the capital as 'evidence.' Emotional beat: rising dread; the record itself is about to be confiscated.

chapters.title: A Forgery Worth Making
chapters.summary: Rosalind and Elias together. They plan to build a decoy wheel — perfect, plausible, wrong — while Rosalind decodes the true one. Working side by side through nights, the romance becomes undeniable. Emotional beat: love as conspiracy; tenderness sharpened by stakes.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Mercy
chapters.summary: Magistrate's POV. The local magistrate, revealed as a man who signed the cover-up out of fear years ago, discovers the plan — and hesitates. His chapters show the machinery of ordinary cowardice. Emotional beat: moral vertigo; even the compromised want absolution.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The decoy is discovered because someone informed — the guild's own agent in town. Elias is detained; the real wheel is seized from the dome. Rosalind escapes with only her decoded notes sewn into her coat lining. Emotional beat: devastation; everything built in snow and lamplight collapses in an afternoon.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Hiding in Marta's cellar, Rosalind confronts the theme directly: she cannot carry the clock, the dome, or Elias's freedom — only the record. She transcribes the decoded data onto the guild certificate itself, hiding truth inside the document she was ordered to sign. Emotional beat: resolve forged from loss.

chapters.title: The Thaw
chapters.summary: Elias's POV, imprisoned. Elias endures interrogation, giving nothing, sustained by the certainty that Rosalind got out. The bridge reopens; prisoners and evidence are to be transported together. Emotional beat: endurance as devotion; hope measured in drips of melting ice.

chapters.title: Crossing at Flood
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Against every instruction, Rosalind returns across the just-reopened bridge during flood warnings to intercept the transport — choosing both the man and the record, refusing the false choice. Emotional beat: the book's thesis made flesh; love and duty reconciled by courage.

chapters.title: The Hearing at the Guildhall
chapters.summary: Climax, multiple POVs. In the capital's guildhall, before the victors' historians, Rosalind presents the certificate, the notebook, and her testimony as the transport arrives with Elias and the seized wheel — which she proves authentic by reading its etchings aloud against the clock striking the true hour. The magistrate, finally, corroborates. Emotional beat: climax as public reckoning; time itself testifies.

chapters.title: Verdicts and Repairs
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Aftermath: Anselm's charts enter the record; the magistrate resigns; the guild offers Rosalind partnership contingent on discretion — she declines. Elias is freed but broken in ways silence can't fix quickly. Emotional beat: victory with a limp; justice entered, not completed.

chapters.title: Spring Calibration
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Back at the observatory, Rosalind and Elias recalibrate the master clock together, replacing the wheel with a new one bearing Anselm's data etched openly, for anyone to read. Quiet scenes of two people learning to be off-duty. Emotional beat: healing as slow craft; love without secrecy for the first time.

chapters.title: The Hour It Was Always Meant to Strike
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, coda years later. Rosalind, now the observatory's clockkeeper, trains an apprentice girl who asks why the clock matters so much. Rosalind answers with the story's creed: instruments remember what people are made to forget. The clock strikes; the valley keeps its true time. Emotional beat: resolution as transmission — memory passed hand to hand, gear to gear.
